key_insight: Professionals and patient representatives saw potential for LLMs in general practice, prioritizing consultation summaries and triage while differing in their preferred applications.
clinical_relevance: LLM implementation should reflect role-specific needs and demonstrate workload benefits without compromising safety, personal care, or accessibility.
method: Semi-structured interviews with 31 participants in the Netherlands: 12 GPs, 7 GP assistants, 6 practice nurses, and 6 patient representatives.
Participants discussed and prioritized 21 LLM applications across five practice domains.
Transcripts underwent combined deductive and inductive qualitative analysis.
evidence_signal: Consultation summaries and triage/urgency classification received the highest reported priority ratings (18/31; 58%); interviews assessed preferences, not clinical effectiveness.
watch_item: Perceived usefulness does not establish workload reduction: LLM errors and review demands could create extra work, and simpler tools may suffice.
paper_title: Applications of large language model in general practice: a qualitative interview study with professionals and patients
